blocks.en: 📖 Bible Characters II — Unit 3: Jeremiah — The Weeping Prophet Who Stayed Faithful
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Personajes de la Biblia II — Unidad 3: Jeremías — El Profeta que Lloró pero Permaneció Fiel

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you; before you were born I sanctified you; I ordained you a prophet to the nations." — Jeremiah 1:5 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Antes que te formase en el vientre te conocí, y antes que salieses de la matriz te santifiqué, te di por profeta a las naciones.» — Jeremías 1:5 (RVG)

blocks.en: Some servants of God are remembered for their victories; Jeremiah is remembered for his tears. For some forty years he preached to a nation that would not listen, watched his warnings come true in fire and chains, and wept over a people who hated him for loving them enough to tell the truth. He was beaten, mocked, imprisoned, and once lowered into a muddy pit to die — and still he would not stop speaking for God. He is called the weeping prophet, but he might just as fairly be called the faithful prophet, for his life answers one of the hardest questions a believer can face: how do we keep serving God when no one is listening and faithfulness costs everything?
blocks.es_reference: Algunos siervos de Dios son recordados por sus victorias; Jeremías es recordado por sus lágrimas. Durante unos cuarenta años predicó a una nación que no quería escuchar, vio sus advertencias cumplirse en fuego y cadenas, y lloró por un pueblo que lo odiaba por amarlo lo suficiente como para decirle la verdad. Fue azotado, burlado, encarcelado, y una vez descendido a un pozo fangoso para morir —y aun así no quiso dejar de hablar por Dios—. Se le llama el profeta llorón, pero con igual justicia podría llamarse el profeta fiel, porque su vida responde a una de las preguntas más difíciles que un creyente puede enfrentar: ¿cómo seguimos sirviendo a Dios cuando nadie escucha y la fidelidad lo cuesta todo?

blocks.en: Subject: Jeremiah — the weeping prophet who stayed faithful.
blocks.es_reference: Tema: Jeremías — el profeta que lloró pero permaneció fiel.

blocks.en: Proposition: God equips the servants He calls, and true faithfulness keeps speaking and trusting even when the message is rejected and the cost is high, looking ahead to the new covenant of grace.
blocks.es_reference: Proposición: Dios equipa a los siervos que llama, y la verdadera fidelidad sigue hablando y confiando aun cuando el mensaje es rechazado y el precio es alto, mirando hacia el nuevo pacto de gracia.

blocks.en: We will trace five movements in the life of Jeremiah.
blocks.es_reference: Trazaremos cinco movimientos en la vida de Jeremías.

blocks.en: I. The Call of a Boy
blocks.es_reference: I. El Llamado de un Joven

blocks.en: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah while he was still young — and in truth it had come even before he was born.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra de Jehová vino a Jeremías cuando aún era joven —y en verdad había venido aun antes de que naciera—.

blocks.en: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you; before you were born I sanctified you; I ordained you a prophet to the nations. (Jeremiah 1:5, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Antes que te formase en el vientre te conocí, y antes que salieses de la matriz te santifiqué, te di por profeta a las naciones. (Jeremías 1:5, RVG)

blocks.en: God knew this boy intimately and had set him apart for a holy task long before he drew his first breath. Jeremiah's reaction was not eagerness but fear: "Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I cannot speak, for I am a youth." God brushed the excuse aside — "Do not say, 'I am a youth,' for you shall go to all to whom I send you... Do not be afraid... for I am with you to deliver you" — and then He reached out and touched Jeremiah's mouth, saying, "Behold, I have put My words in your mouth."
blocks.es_reference: Dios conocía íntimamente a este joven y lo había apartado para una tarea santa mucho antes de que respirara por primera vez. La reacción de Jeremías no fue entusiasmo sino temor: «¡Ah, Señor Jehová! He aquí, no sé hablar, porque soy niño». Dios apartó la excusa —«No digas: Soy niño; porque a todo lo que te envíe irás... No temas... porque contigo estoy para librarte»— y entonces extendió la mano y tocó la boca de Jeremías, diciendo: «He aquí he puesto mis palabras en tu boca».

blocks.en: Two lessons shine here. First, God loves to call ordinary and unlikely people — the young, the timid, those certain they cannot do it — and then He equips them; the same God who issues the call also supplies the words and the strength to obey it. If God calls us, He will furnish what the calling requires. Second, there is a difference between a single task and a lifelong call. Jeremiah was not handed one errand to finish and then walk away from; he was claimed for a lifetime. He hesitated precisely because he glimpsed the cost. And God's answer was not the promise of an easy road, but of a sufficient presence: "I am with you."
blocks.es_reference: Dos lecciones brillan aquí. Primera, a Dios le encanta llamar a personas comunes e improbables —los jóvenes, los tímidos, los que están seguros de que no pueden hacerlo— y luego los equipa; el mismo Dios que da el llamado también suple las palabras y la fuerza para obedecerlo. Si Dios nos llama, proveerá lo que el llamado requiera. Segunda, hay una diferencia entre una sola tarea y un llamado de por vida. A Jeremías no se le entregó un encargo para terminarlo y luego alejarse; fue reclamado para toda una vida. Vaciló precisamente porque vislumbró el costo. Y la respuesta de Dios no fue la promesa de un camino fácil, sino de una presencia suficiente: «Contigo estoy».

blocks.en: There is real comfort in this for anyone who has ever felt too small for what God asks. Jeremiah's qualification was never his eloquence or his age; it was the God who stood behind him. We are tempted to measure a calling by our own resources and conclude we are not enough — and we are right, we are not. But the call of God never rests on the strength of the one called; it rests on the faithfulness of the One who calls. He does not send us out empty. The mouth He opens, He also fills; the task He assigns, He also enables. Our part is simply to go and to trust.
blocks.es_reference: Hay verdadero consuelo en esto para cualquiera que alguna vez se haya sentido demasiado pequeño para lo que Dios pide. La calificación de Jeremías nunca fue su elocuencia ni su edad; era el Dios que estaba detrás de él. Somos tentados a medir un llamado por nuestros propios recursos y concluir que no somos suficientes —y tenemos razón, no lo somos—. Pero el llamado de Dios nunca descansa en la fuerza del llamado; descansa en la fidelidad de Aquel que llama. No nos envía vacíos. La boca que abre, también la llena; la tarea que asigna, también la capacita. Nuestra parte es simplemente ir y confiar.

blocks.en: II. The Unwelcome Message
blocks.es_reference: II. El Mensaje No Bienvenido

blocks.en: Jeremiah preached through the last years of the kingdom of Judah, under a succession of kings, down to the very day Babylon burned Jerusalem to the ground. His message was deeply unpopular. The nation had forsaken the living God for idols, and unless they repented, judgment was coming. To make the point unforgettable, God sent the prophet down to a potter's house.
blocks.es_reference: Jeremías predicó durante los últimos años del reino de Judá, bajo una sucesión de reyes, hasta el día mismo en que Babilonia quemó Jerusalén hasta los cimientos. Su mensaje era muy impopular. La nación había abandonado al Dios vivo por los ídolos, y a menos que se arrepintieran, el juicio venía. Para grabar el punto, Dios envió al profeta a la casa de un alfarero.

blocks.en: "O house of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter?" says the LORD. "Look, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand." (Jeremiah 18:6, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: ¿No podré yo hacer de vosotros como este alfarero, oh casa de Israel? dice Jehová. He aquí que como el barro en la mano del alfarero, así sois vosotros en mi mano. (Jeremías 18:6, RVG)

blocks.en: As the potter takes a marred lump and patiently reshapes it into something useful, so God could yet reshape a repentant people if only they would yield. Jeremiah's commission, spoken at his call, had been twofold — "to root out and to pull down... to build and to plant." First came the hard word of warning, the tearing down of false hopes and proud sins; but beyond the judgment lay a word of rebuilding and planting. Again and again Jeremiah pleaded with Judah to turn back to God before it was too late. The warnings of God are never the cruelty of a harsh judge; they are the last mercy of a Father still calling His children home.
blocks.es_reference: Como el alfarero toma una masa estropeada y pacientemente la rehace en algo útil, así Dios podía aún rehacer a un pueblo arrepentido si tan solo cedía. La comisión de Jeremías, dada en su llamado, había sido doble —«para arrancar y para destruir... para edificar y para plantar»—. Primero vino la palabra dura de advertencia, el derribar de las falsas esperanzas y los pecados soberbios; pero más allá del juicio había una palabra de reedificar y plantar. Una y otra vez Jeremías rogó a Judá que se volviera a Dios antes de que fuera demasiado tarde. Las advertencias de Dios nunca son la crueldad de un juez severo; son la última misericordia de un Padre que todavía llama a sus hijos a casa.

blocks.en: The potter's house holds a tender truth about God. The clay had been marred, yet the potter did not throw it away — he worked it again into another vessel, as it seemed good to him. So God deals with failing people. Judgment was never His first desire or His final word; His longing was always that the nation would soften in His hands and let Him remake them. That patience is the reason Jeremiah preached at all. A God eager only to destroy would have sent no prophet; He sends warnings precisely because He is not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
blocks.es_reference: La casa del alfarero guarda una verdad tierna acerca de Dios. El barro había sido estropeado, y sin embargo el alfarero no lo desechó —lo volvió a labrar en otra vasija, como mejor le pareció—. Así trata Dios con la gente que falla. El juicio nunca fue su primer deseo ni su última palabra; su anhelo siempre fue que la nación se ablandara en sus manos y le dejara rehacerla. Esa paciencia es la razón por la que Jeremías predicaba. Un Dios ansioso solo de destruir no habría enviado profeta; envía advertencias precisamente porque no quiere que ninguno perezca, sino que todos vengan al arrepentimiento.

blocks.en: III. The Weeping Prophet
blocks.es_reference: III. El Profeta que Lloró

blocks.en: Judah would not listen. And the man who faithfully carried God's word paid a bitter price for it. Jeremiah was clamped in the stocks, beaten, accused of treason, and threatened with death. Once he was let down by ropes into a miry cistern, where he sank into the mud and was left to die, until a foreigner in the king's court begged for his life. On another day the king took the scroll of Jeremiah's prophecies, cut it to pieces with a penknife, and threw it into the fire. Through all of it the prophet grieved — not chiefly for himself, but for a people racing headlong toward ruin.
blocks.es_reference: Judá no quiso escuchar. Y el hombre que fielmente llevaba la palabra de Dios pagó un precio amargo por ello. Jeremías fue puesto en el cepo, azotado, acusado de traición y amenazado de muerte. Una vez lo bajaron con sogas a una cisterna fangosa, donde se hundió en el lodo y fue dejado para morir, hasta que un extranjero en la corte del rey rogó por su vida. Otro día el rey tomó el rollo de las profecías de Jeremías, lo cortó en pedazos con un cortaplumas y lo echó al fuego. A través de todo ello el profeta se afligía —no principalmente por sí mismo, sino por un pueblo que corría de cabeza hacia la ruina—.

blocks.en: Oh, that my head were waters, and my eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people! (Jeremiah 9:1, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: ¡Oh, si mi cabeza se hiciese aguas, y mis ojos fuentes de lágrimas, para que llorara día y noche los muertos de la hija de mi pueblo! (Jeremías 9:1, RVG)

blocks.en: Here is the very heart of a true prophet, and of every faithful servant of God: he loved the people who rejected him. Jeremiah never announced judgment with cold satisfaction; he wept over it. This is the balance so easily lost. To speak hard truth without love is mere cruelty; to love without ever speaking the truth is cowardice dressed up as kindness. Jeremiah did both at once — he told Judah exactly what they did not want to hear, and it broke his heart to do it. The tears of the prophet were the proof that the warnings of the prophet were spoken in love.
blocks.es_reference: Aquí está el corazón mismo de un verdadero profeta, y de todo siervo fiel de Dios: amó al pueblo que lo rechazó. Jeremías nunca anunció el juicio con fría satisfacción; lloró sobre él. Este es el equilibrio tan fácilmente perdido. Hablar verdad dura sin amor es mera crueldad; amar sin jamás hablar la verdad es cobardía disfrazada de bondad. Jeremías hizo ambas cosas a la vez —le dijo a Judá exactamente lo que no quería oír, y le rompió el corazón hacerlo—. Las lágrimas del profeta eran la prueba de que las advertencias del profeta se hablaban con amor.

blocks.en: We should let Jeremiah's example correct two common errors. Some imagine that faithfulness to God means being harsh, and they wound people in the name of truth. Others imagine that love means never saying anything uncomfortable, and they watch people walk toward ruin without a word. Jeremiah shows a better way. He delivered the hardest message of his generation, and he delivered it soaked in tears. The truth he spoke was true; the love he felt was real; and the two were never at war in him. That is the costly, Christlike combination every servant of God is called to: full of grace and full of truth at the same time.
blocks.es_reference: Dejemos que el ejemplo de Jeremías corrija dos errores comunes. Algunos imaginan que la fidelidad a Dios significa ser duros, y hieren a la gente en nombre de la verdad. Otros imaginan que el amor significa nunca decir nada incómodo, y observan a la gente caminar hacia la ruina sin una palabra. Jeremías muestra un camino mejor. Entregó el mensaje más difícil de su generación, y lo entregó empapado en lágrimas. La verdad que habló era verdadera; el amor que sintió era real; y los dos nunca estuvieron en guerra en él. Esa es la combinación costosa y semejante a Cristo a la que todo siervo de Dios es llamado: lleno de gracia y de verdad a la vez.

blocks.en: IV. The Fire in His Bones
blocks.es_reference: IV. El Fuego en sus Huesos

blocks.en: At last the strain grew almost unbearable. Jeremiah had poured out his whole life on a message that brought him nothing but suffering, and there came a day when he resolved to quit — to close his mouth and never speak in God's name again. But he discovered that he could not.
blocks.es_reference: Al fin la tensión se hizo casi insoportable. Jeremías había derramado toda su vida en un mensaje que no le traía sino sufrimiento, y llegó un día en que resolvió renunciar —cerrar su boca y no volver a hablar jamás en el nombre de Dios—. Pero descubrió que no podía.

blocks.en: Then I said, "I will not make mention of Him, nor speak anymore in His name." But His word was in my heart like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I was weary of holding it back, and I could not. (Jeremiah 20:9, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Y dije: No me acordaré más de él, ni hablaré más en su nombre; pero había en mi corazón como un fuego ardiente metido en mis huesos; traté de sufrirlo, y no pude. (Jeremías 20:9, RVG)

blocks.en: This is one of the surest marks of a genuine call from God: it takes hold of a person and will not let go. Jeremiah could not walk away, because the word of God was burning inside him like a fire he could not smother. When obedience had cost him everything and offered him nothing in return, the call itself became the thing that held him to his post. A servant of God carries on through rejection and weariness not because he is strong in himself, but because God has kindled within him a fire that refuses to go out. What we cannot keep up by willpower, God sustains by His own word living in us.
blocks.es_reference: Esta es una de las señales más seguras de un llamado genuino de Dios: se apodera de una persona y no la suelta. Jeremías no podía alejarse, porque la palabra de Dios ardía dentro de él como un fuego que no podía sofocar. Cuando la obediencia le había costado todo y no le ofrecía nada a cambio, el llamado mismo se volvió lo que lo mantenía en su puesto. Un siervo de Dios sigue adelante a través del rechazo y el cansancio no porque sea fuerte en sí mismo, sino porque Dios ha encendido dentro de él un fuego que se niega a apagarse. Lo que no podemos mantener por fuerza de voluntad, Dios lo sostiene por su propia palabra viviendo en nosotros.

blocks.en: Notice, too, that faithfulness is not measured by visible success. By every outward standard, Jeremiah's ministry looked like failure: the people did not repent, the city fell, and tradition says he died in exile among a people who still would not listen. Yet heaven did not count him a failure, for he had been faithful. We are not responsible for how others respond to God's word; we are responsible only to be faithful in delivering it. The results belong to God. A servant who speaks the truth in love and is rejected has still succeeded in the only thing God asked of him — he was faithful at his post.
blocks.es_reference: Note, además, que la fidelidad no se mide por el éxito visible. Según toda norma externa, el ministerio de Jeremías parecía un fracaso: el pueblo no se arrepintió, la ciudad cayó, y la tradición dice que murió en el exilio entre un pueblo que todavía no quería escuchar. Sin embargo, el cielo no lo contó como fracaso, porque había sido fiel. No somos responsables de cómo otros respondan a la palabra de Dios; somos responsables solo de ser fieles al entregarla. Los resultados pertenecen a Dios. Un siervo que habla la verdad en amor y es rechazado aún ha tenido éxito en lo único que Dios le pidió —fue fiel en su puesto—.

blocks.en: V. The New Covenant
blocks.es_reference: V. El Nuevo Pacto

blocks.en: Yet Jeremiah's message was never only judgment. Even as the Babylonian armies closed in, God told him to buy a field in his hometown of Anathoth and have the deed sealed before witnesses — a strange, costly act of hope, a public sign that one day God's people would return and houses and fields would be bought again in the land. And to this weeping prophet God entrusted one of the most radiant promises in all the Old Testament.
blocks.es_reference: Sin embargo, el mensaje de Jeremías nunca fue solo juicio. Aun mientras los ejércitos babilonios se acercaban, Dios le dijo que comprara un campo en su pueblo natal de Anatot e hiciera sellar la escritura ante testigos —un acto extraño y costoso de esperanza, una señal pública de que un día el pueblo de Dios volvería y se comprarían de nuevo casas y campos en la tierra—. Y a este profeta que lloraba Dios le confió una de las promesas más radiantes de todo el Antiguo Testamento.

blocks.en: I will put My law in their minds, and write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people... For I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more. (Jeremiah 31:33-34, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Daré mi ley en su mente, y la escribiré en su corazón; y yo seré a ellos por Dios, y ellos me serán por pueblo... porque perdonaré la maldad de ellos, y no me acordaré más de su pecado. (Jeremías 31:33-34, RVG)

blocks.en: This is the new covenant — and it is the gospel held out in promise centuries before it came. The old covenant had been carved on tablets of stone and broken again and again by a stubborn people; the new covenant God Himself would write inside the human heart, and seal it with full and final forgiveness. On the night before He died, Jesus lifted the cup and said to His disciples, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood." Everything Jeremiah longed for — sins forgiven and remembered no more, God's law no longer a heavy weight pressing from the outside but a delight written within — comes to us through Christ, and it is received not by our performance but by grace through faith.
blocks.es_reference: Este es el nuevo pacto —y es el evangelio extendido en promesa siglos antes de que viniera—. El antiguo pacto había sido grabado en tablas de piedra y quebrantado una y otra vez por un pueblo terco; el nuevo pacto Dios mismo lo escribiría dentro del corazón humano, y lo sellaría con perdón pleno y definitivo. La noche antes de morir, Jesús levantó la copa y dijo a sus discípulos: «Esta copa es el nuevo pacto en mi sangre». Todo lo que Jeremías anhelaba —los pecados perdonados y no recordados más, la ley de Dios ya no un peso pesado oprimiendo desde fuera sino un deleite escrito dentro— viene a nosotros por medio de Cristo, y se recibe no por nuestro desempeño sino por gracia por medio de la fe.

blocks.en: How fitting that the prophet of judgment was given the brightest gospel promise in the Old Testament. The same man who wept over a doomed city was allowed to see, centuries in advance, the day when God would forgive sins and remember them no more. This is how God works: He does not leave His people in the rubble of their failure but points them to grace beyond it. Jeremiah could not yet name the cross, but he saw its effect — a clean heart, a forgiven people, a law written within by the Spirit of God. What he glimpsed in shadow, we now hold in the full light of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Qué apropiado que al profeta del juicio se le diera la promesa del evangelio más brillante del Antiguo Testamento. El mismo hombre que lloró sobre una ciudad condenada pudo ver, siglos por adelantado, el día en que Dios perdonaría los pecados y no se acordaría más de ellos. Así obra Dios: no deja a su pueblo en los escombros de su fracaso sino que lo señala a la gracia más allá de él. Jeremías no podía aún nombrar la cruz, pero vio su efecto —un corazón limpio, un pueblo perdonado, una ley escrita dentro por el Espíritu de Dios—. Lo que vislumbró en sombra, nosotros lo tenemos ahora a plena luz de Cristo.

blocks.en: So Jeremiah leaves us a double inheritance. He teaches us how to be faithful: God equips the ones He calls, real faithfulness keeps speaking the truth in love even when no one listens, and a genuine call burns on through every discouragement and every cost. And he points us forward: past all the tears and the ruin, to a God who writes His law on willing hearts and remembers our sins no more. The weeping prophet wept because he could see the judgment bearing down; but he also saw, far off on the horizon, the dawn of grace — and that grace has now come to us in Jesus Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Así que Jeremías nos deja una doble herencia. Nos enseña cómo ser fieles: Dios equipa a los que llama, la verdadera fidelidad sigue hablando la verdad en amor aun cuando nadie escucha, y un llamado genuino arde a través de todo desánimo y todo costo. Y nos señala hacia adelante: más allá de todas las lágrimas y la ruina, hacia un Dios que escribe su ley en corazones dispuestos y no se acuerda más de nuestros pecados. El profeta que lloró lloró porque podía ver el juicio que se avecinaba; pero también vio, lejos en el horizonte, el amanecer de la gracia —y esa gracia ha venido ahora a nosotros en Jesucristo—.

fill.prompt: God told Jeremiah, "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you; before you were born I ____ you" (Jeremiah 1:5).
Jeremiah's first excuse was, "Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I cannot speak, for I am a ____."
At the potter's house God said, "As the ____ is in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand" (Jeremiah 18:6).
Once Jeremiah was let down by ropes into a miry ____, where he sank into the mud and was left to die.
The king cut the scroll of Jeremiah's prophecies to pieces with a ____ and threw it into the fire.
The weeping prophet cried, "Oh, that my head were waters, and my eyes a fountain of ____" (Jeremiah 9:1).
When Jeremiah resolved to quit, God's word was in his heart "like a burning fire shut up in my ____" (Jeremiah 20:9).
As the Babylonian armies closed in, God told Jeremiah to buy a field in his hometown of ____ as a sign of hope.
In the new covenant God promised, "I will put My law in their minds, and write it on their ____" (Jeremiah 31:33).
On the night before He died, Jesus lifted the cup and said, "This cup is the new ____ in My blood."

sa.prompt: Trace the five movements of Jeremiah's life and ministry.
sa.model: Jeremiah's life moves through five stages. He received his call as a youth, knew and set apart before birth, and God promised to equip him. He carried an unwelcome message to Judah, shown at the potter's house that God could reshape a repentant nation. As the weeping prophet he wept over the people who rejected him. When he tried to quit, God's word was a fire shut up in his bones, and he could not stop. At last he announced the new covenant of grace, and through it all he stayed faithful.

sa.prompt: Describe Jeremiah's call and his objection, and how God answered.
sa.model: God said He knew Jeremiah in the womb and had set him apart before birth to be a prophet. Jeremiah objected that he was only a youth and could not speak. God answered, 'Do not say, I am a youth... do not be afraid, for I am with you,' and He touched his mouth and put His words in it. This teaches that God calls ordinary and unlikely people and then equips them; the One who calls also supplies the words and strength to obey.

sa.prompt: What was Jeremiah's message to Judah, and what did the potter's house illustrate?
sa.model: Jeremiah's message was that judgment was coming on Judah because they had forsaken God for idols, unless they would repent. At the potter's house God showed that just as the potter reshapes a marred lump of clay, He could reshape a repentant nation still in His hand. His warning was not the cruelty of a harsh judge but the last mercy of a Father calling His children home, urging them to turn back before it was too late.

sa.prompt: Why is Jeremiah called the weeping prophet?
sa.model: Jeremiah is called the weeping prophet because he wept day and night over his people, longing that his eyes were a fountain of tears for the slain of his nation. He did not announce judgment with cold satisfaction; he grieved over it, for he loved the very people who rejected him. His tears show the right balance: he spoke hard truth, but always in love. To speak truth without love is cruelty, and to love without truth is cowardice; Jeremiah did both.

sa.prompt: What did Jeremiah's suffering and rejection look like?
sa.model: Jeremiah suffered greatly for his faithfulness. He was put in the stocks, beaten, accused of treason, and threatened with death. Once he was lowered by ropes into a miry cistern, where he sank in the mud and was left to die until a foreigner begged for his life. The king cut his scroll to pieces and burned it in the fire. Through all this rejection, the prophet kept speaking God's word, grieving more for his people than for himself.

sa.prompt: What does "a burning fire shut up in my bones" reveal about Jeremiah's call?
sa.model: Worn down by suffering, Jeremiah resolved to quit and never speak in God's name again, but he found that he could not. God's word was like a burning fire shut up in his bones; he was weary of holding it back and could not. This reveals a sure mark of a genuine call: it takes hold of a person and will not let go. What a servant cannot keep up by willpower, God sustains by His own word burning within, holding him to his post.

sa.prompt: What sign of hope did God give through the field at Anathoth?
sa.model: Even as the Babylonian army closed in, God told Jeremiah to buy a field in his hometown of Anathoth and have the deed sealed before witnesses. It was a costly, public sign of hope, declaring that one day God's people would return and houses and fields would be bought again in the land. In the very shadow of ruin, Jeremiah signed a deed of hope, showing that beyond the judgment God intended to restore His people.

sa.prompt: What is the new covenant God promised through Jeremiah (Jer 31:33-34)?
sa.model: Through Jeremiah God promised a new covenant: He would put His law in their minds and write it on their hearts, and He would be their God and they His people. Best of all, He promised, 'I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more.' Unlike the old covenant carved on stone and broken, this covenant God would write inside the heart and seal with full forgiveness — the gospel of grace held out in promise.

sa.prompt: How does the new covenant point to Christ and the gospel?
sa.model: The new covenant points straight to Christ. On the night before He died, Jesus lifted the cup and said, 'This cup is the new covenant in My blood.' Everything Jeremiah promised — sins forgiven and remembered no more, God's law written within rather than pressing from outside — is fulfilled in Christ. And it is received not by our performance but by grace through faith. What Jeremiah saw far off as a promise comes to us in the gospel of Jesus.

sa.prompt: What does Jeremiah teach believers about faithfulness to God's call?
sa.model: Jeremiah teaches that God equips the ones He calls, so we need not fear our weakness. True faithfulness keeps speaking the truth in love even when no one will listen, and it perseveres through rejection and suffering. A genuine call burns on through every discouragement and cost, sustained by God's own word within. Faithfulness is measured not by results or applause but by staying at the post God gave us, trusting Him to the end.
